dct_description_sm: Through their lives humans accumulate persistent environmental contaminants in their body raising scientific health concerns and the need to investigate potential health consequences.  Methymercury (MeHg), polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), and organochlorine pesticides (OCP), are present in the Northern regions and these chemicals were detected in tissues of Northern communities.  Based on their human serum profiles, Bowers' laboratory reconstituted a mixture of these three chemical groups [Chu et al., 2008. J. Toxicol Environ Health A 71(2), 93-108].  Using the rat as a laboratory model, the purpose of this research project is to (1) generate new information on the toxicity of this complex mixture of 'Northern Contaminants', and its components (MeHg, PCBs, OCP), and (2) use this information to initiate a cross-fostering experiment to investigate effects related to only in utero exposure, or to only lactational exposure, and those induced by both lactational and in utero exposure to the mixture of 'Northern contaminants'. In addition, groups of rats will be included to test modulating effects of aryl hydrocarbon receptor agonists (polychlorinated dibenzodioxins, polychlorinated dibenzofurans, and non-ortho-PCBs) on the toxicity of the 'Northern contaminants' mixture.
dct_subject_sm: Health sciences and contaminants -> Persistent organic pollutants (POPs)
dct_title_s: Effects of exposure to mixtures of environmental contaminants during the in utero and/or the postnatal developmental period in the rat
